selection.why: This plan has the strongest median case-span reduction at -36.7368% and nearly the strongest waiting reduction at -63.8792%, while mean duration, service, and utilisation all show significant measured changes without a significant worsening under the computed rule. It is cleaner than the alternatives because it removes CA-002's significant worsening contribution.
selection.gain_reading: both: service fell 86.9610% and waiting fell 63.8792%, so the redesign reflects both less work being done and less queueing. The payload does not provide absolute case-hours for those two measures, but its attributable activity change is -10.7972 h/case net; that activity-hour figure is not directly comparable with case-span hours.

selection.runner_up: round2 — I would otherwise have taken it for the stronger service reduction (-89.2860%) and utilisation reduction (-40.7899%), but it costs a weaker median (-34.2923%), weaker waiting reduction (-62.9636%), and retains CA-002, whose own attributable effect worsens activity time by +1.0089 h/case.
selection.caveat: Do not read the large service reduction as faster execution of the same work: the gain source is both, and the case-outcome mix changes materially, with 479 cases per run ending somewhere different. The measured averages do not establish whether those changed outcomes are desirable, and several retained candidates have only shared or simulator-invisible evidence rather than standalone attribution.

compliance_final.note: DECISIONS B: judged on prior knowledge alone and never overturnable by measurement. This ruling decides what the deliverable may contain; measurements of plans it bars are kept under `excluded_as_non_compliant` so the cost of the block can still be read.

note: `best` is the best MEASUREMENT in the run, which is usually not the last round. ⚠️ `statistically_tied_with_best` is the SELECTOR'S CANDIDATE POOL, not a set of indistinguishable results: a row is admitted either because it is not significantly worse than `best` on the median, or because it is decisively better on ONE directional measure while possibly far worse on the others. Read each row's `admitted_because` before describing it, and never call the list a tie. `per_candidate` is the winning plan's own account: what each surviving candidate contributed on waiting, duration, throughput and resources.
